forks.then: Disinflation validated — December hike odds slip, crowded USD longs unwind, DXY gives back a percent, gold re-arms toward $4,300.
The October hike revives — December gets fully priced, DXY breaks out above the 18-month top, real yields jump and gold slides back toward $4,000.
The market reads through it — core is the Fed's number; the dollar's first reaction fades by the London close.

setup.consensus: 3.6% y/y (Reuters poll 3.7%), 0.6% m/m; core 0.2% m/m, 2.5% y/y

stakes: Decides whether the October 27–28 hike comes back to life — and whether $35.5bn of crowded dollar longs get to keep the trade.
story_so_far: August CPI surprised hot at 3.4% y/y — and the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75–4.00% in September, with the board warning that AI-boom demand and wealth-effect spending are lodging inflation in the 2.5–3.0% range.

September payrolls then collapsed to 29k — the labor floor cracked. The market split the difference: one more hike in 2026 stays the base case, but the October 27–28 meeting is priced as a hold (~77%).

Into the print the Fed chorus divided openly: Hammack said rates 'need to move higher'; Waller said surging long yields are doing some of the Fed's tightening work; Williams capped 2027 at no further hikes.
Now September CPI is the tiebreaker. Core m/m is the number the market is actually trading: 0.2% or below validates disinflation, 0.3% or hotter revives the October hike nobody has priced.
title: US CPI (Sep)
watch: 7:30 AM CT — CPI prints (BLS); the page flips to live by itself
7:30–8:00 AM CT — first repricing: FedWatch odds, DXY, the 2-year yield
12:30 PM CT — Barkin speaks into the print's aftermath
1:00 PM CT — Fed Beige Book: the anecdotal read on business price hikes
2:00 PM CT — Goolsbee speaks (warned AI inflation is 'jumping out of its lane')

recap.outcome: Hot: core 0.3% m/m (vs 0.2% exp) and 2.6% y/y (vs 2.5% exp) — beats on both core measures; headline 3.7% y/y (vs 3.6% LSEG est, in line with Reuters poll 3.7%) on +0.6% m/m. Energy drove the headline, but core means pressure is broadening.
recap.expected: 3.6% y/y (Reuters poll 3.7%), 0.6% m/m; core 0.2% m/m, 2.5% y/y
recap.pricing: October 27–28 hike back in play (was ~23% priced pre-print; December ~84%). USD bid post-print: EUR/USD slid ~1.1208 → 1.1134 (-0.6%), USD/JPY rose ~158.2 → 158.84 (+0.3%).

thesis.note: The October-hold base case (~77% priced) broke — hot core on both measures revives the October hike the market had shelved; the 'one more hike, but in December' framing shifts toward 'possibly October'.
